title: Bounded complexes inherit a common amplitude from their terms in their actual degrees
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $K^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and $r,s,a,b\in\mathbf Z$. In a chosen derived category [def-pc-derived-category], assume $K^n=0$ for $n<r$ or $s<n$. For each $r\le n\le s$, assume the module $K^n$ placed in cochain degree $n$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, meaning that its derived tensor with every module in degree zero has zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$. Then $K^\bullet$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ in the same sense. No ordering of either pair of endpoints, flatness, or finite generation is assumed.

source.place: Tag 066H, lemma-tor-amplitude-finite-complex; Tags 066K, lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings, and 0655. Sources checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066H and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K.

proof.text: For any extension-closed, isomorphism-closed object property on the homotopy category containing zero, induct on the width of a bounded complex using its degreewise split stupid-truncation triangle. The one-term complex is isomorphic to the single complex in its actual degree. The two truncations have smaller width and their surviving terms are isomorphic to original terms. For an empty interval all terms are zero and hence the complex is zero. This induction is written and proved as bounded_mem_of_single_terms with the proved upstream stupid-truncation, splitting, and single-complex isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 066H, lemma-tor-amplitude-finite-complex; Tags 066K, lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings, and 0655. Sources checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066H and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K.

proof.text: Fix a test module M. Choose a K-flat homotopy representative P of M[0]. The derived tensor functor with Qh(P), with its representative-dependent shift comparison, is triangulated by the proved upstream isTriangulated_tensorRightQhObj. Pull the two homology bounds back along Qh followed by this functor. Their intersection contains zero and is extension closed by the canonical t-structure. Apply the proved induction and transport through Qh(P) ≅ M[0] and quotientCompQhIso. No global tensor-shift instance with a tied derived/Grothendieck universe is used.

theorem bounded_torAmplitude_of_single_terms
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (r s a b : ℤ)
    (hdegrees : ∀ n : ℤ, n < r ∨ s < n → IsZero (K.X n))
    (hterms : ∀ n : ℤ, r ≤ n → n ≤ s →
      DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u} R) a b
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj (K.X n))) :
    DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u} R) a b (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)
